solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Admits getting personal over drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: your own things are personal to you
to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: Someone confesses something once a personal matter comes up over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom for confessing, the same as admitting a fault.

clue.text: With time spare, I resolved to walk

indicators.note: a puzzle resolved is worked out anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with spare time decides to go out for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like 'decided' but signals rearranging SPARE and I into RAIPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or aimlessly, a type of walking.

clue.text: Tried that, am fed up, and won't survive?

definitions.meaning: having already experienced something, been there and done it
being utterly weary of something and wanting no more
being done for, facing ruin or death

explanation.surface: A weary person who has tried everything, is sick of it, and fears the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom covers all three senses: past experience, exasperation, and being doomed.

clue.text: Handy instructions?

parts.note: a guidebook of instructions, and also something done by hand, so both senses of handy

explanation.surface: A request for some useful directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook of instructions; the word also means worked by hand, the second sense of handy.

clue.text: Howl miserably, left with nothing through Depression

indicators.note: the second pieces go through the middle of the first
something done miserably is done badly, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone howls wretchedly, abandoned with nothing, sunk in depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' rearranges HOWL to HOLW; 'through' sets L and O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a dip or sunken place in the ground, a physical depression.

clue.text: 'Male Lead in Flop' — big news

indicators.note: to flop is to collapse in a heap, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid splash about a leading man starring in a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flop' looks like part of the gossip headline but rearranges LEAD IN to ADLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Major news stories make the headline, the large-type title at the top of a front page.

clue.text: Gosh! Two maidens in navy, topless!

indicators.note: the maidens go inside the shortened colour
with its top letter removed

parts.note: navy is a shade of blue
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, so two give MM

explanation.surface: A shocked exclamation at two young women in the navy going topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes B from BLUE, leaving LUE; M is a maiden over in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: This old British exclamation of surprise works as an interjection like 'Gosh!'.

clue.text: Made a father, or 'Dad' — champagne gulped, head off

indicators.note: the father figure swallows the shortened drink, so it goes inside
the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A new dad celebrates by gulping champagne until he loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad' is the wordplay's container, not the definition; 'head off' trims the wine and 'gulped' swallows the remainder, INE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordination makes a man a priest, addressed as Father in many churches.

clue.text: Take almost the whole week off from routine

definitions.text: Take almost the whole week off
definitions.meaning: read literally, putting in just one day's labour leaves the other six free

explanation.surface: Someone wants a long break from their usual grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday means ordinary or commonplace, everyday humdrum, like a routine task.

clue.text: Furious with horsehair cover being not natural

indicators.note: the hair covers the angry word, which goes inside it

parts.note: a horse's mane is its long neck hair

explanation.surface: An angry complaint that a horsehair covering is synthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic, artificial things are made by people rather than occurring in nature.

clue.text: What's the point of lace?

parts.note: a sharp point, and the word for lacing a drink with alcohol

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why anyone bothers with lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike is a sharp point, and to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol.

clue.text: A century with a single trickling through — dope!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go through the middle of the outer pair

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: letters trickling run loose and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A batsman's century includes one lucky single scratched through the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trickling' rearranges A SINGLE to NALGESI; 'through' puts it between A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a drug, and a painkiller is a drug given to dull pain.

clue.text: Make the number up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: An instruction to invent a figure or round a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To net is to make or earn as clear profit.

clue.text: Not bad as forged notes?

definitions.meaning: counterfeit banknotes are only useful if they can be passed off as real

explanation.surface: A comment on the quality of some counterfeit money.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate work is acceptable, and fake money good enough to be spent passes muster.

clue.text: Back home, imbibing rum, got sleepy

indicators.note: drinking in, so the second piece goes inside
the word is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a home or lair
rum is old British slang for odd, strange

explanation.surface: Back home after a few rums, someone grows drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is old British slang for strange, not the drink; 'Back' reverses the home word to NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding off is drifting to sleep, the head dropping forward when drowsy.

clue.text: If not love, the wires may have got crossed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: crossed wires are tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A misunderstanding in a romance: maybe there were crossed wires.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean 'or else', introducing what follows in the alternative case.

clue.text: Oddly-shaped mouse traps and not very big

indicators.note: the jumbled rodent letters hold the conjunction inside
the letters are given a strange new form

explanation.surface: Oddly-shaped mousetraps that are not very big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly-shaped' gives EMOUS, and 'traps' is a verb here: the jumbled rodent holds the conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: huge, immense, very large.

clue.text: Little tyke putting on airs is noxious

indicators.note: the solution with airs put on it makes the harmful word, so airs is what is taken away

explanation.surface: A cheeky child giving himself airs is obnoxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer putting on AIRS makes IMPAIRS, which is noxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a little devil, a small demon.

clue.text: Strays. A need, possibly, for wife to curb?

indicators.note: the title restrains the jumbled letters inside it
the letters might possibly form something else

explanation.surface: A husband who strays might need his wife to rein him in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' gives EANDE; 'to curb' means hold in check, so the wife's title encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off course or drift aimlessly, as a river winds.

clue.text: He left these cooked and ready

indicators.note: cooked letters are mixed up
he departing means he is taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: He left these dishes cooked and ready to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes HE from THESE, leaving TSE; 'cooked' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set means prepared, as in 'all set to go'.

clue.text: 'Viewable,' you say, to encourage

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, a sound-alike

explanation.surface: Someone describes something as visible as a way to encourage.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone on to act.

clue.text: Drink 'earty!

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows the dropped H of a Cockney accent, so the synonym loses its H too

explanation.surface: A cheery Cockney toast urging everyone to drink heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearty means HALE; dropping the H, as the apostrophe does, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer, a type of drink, especially a traditional British brew.

clue.text: Lie worked? Not if I will get caught entering

indicators.note: the letter enters the jumbled ones
worked letters are kneaded into new shape

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Did the lie work? Not if I'm caught breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges NOT IF and I into FITION; 'entering' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Invented stories are untrue, so a made-up falsehood is a fiction.

clue.text: Port and soft drink with twist as chaser

indicators.note: a chaser follows, so this piece comes second

parts.note: lime is a soft drink, as in lime cordial
to rick is to wrench or twist a joint

explanation.surface: Someone orders port and a soft drink with a twist of peel to chase it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink; it is the Irish port city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Shannon in Ireland is a port.

clue.text: Pressed on in passion to meet date

indicators.note: the next piece is joined on
the clue says on sits in passion, so that word is placed inside the anger synonym

explanation.surface: Pressed on passionately to meet a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes are pressed with an iron, so smoothed with heat is the same.

clue.text: Letter crosses

parts.note: the X marks at the end of a letter stand for ...

explanation.definitionFit: Crosses written as X at the foot of a letter stand for affectionate pecks.

clue.text: Compere's here and about to make a comeback

definitions.note: Compere's means the compere is, a noun

indicators.note: coming back means read backwards

explanation.surface: The compere is here and about to stage a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere hosts a show, and a host who introduces acts is a presenter.

clue.text: Found more than half ruined: destitute

indicators.note: ruined letters are knocked about
five of the nine letters, a little more than half

explanation.surface: Someone discovered more than half ruined and penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half' takes DESTI from DESTITUTE; 'ruined' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Founding a building is locating it; sited means placed or established.

clue.text: Quantities of juice non-drinker had been swallowing

indicators.note: the verb takes in the abstainer

parts.note: was stands for had been in many sentences

explanation.surface: A teetotaller has been drinking quantities of fruit juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juice' is slang for electricity, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is slang for electric power, measured in units of power.

clue.text: Doesn't like the inside also being remodelled

indicators.note: remodelling reshapes, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the inside also being remodelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' first builds ALTHESO, which 'being remodelled' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Detests strongly; hating is a stronger form of not liking.

clue.text: Stem broken and missing case that's precious

definitions.note: a noun phrase, something that is precious

indicators.note: the word is a case round the broken letters
broken letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken stem, and a missing case for something precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' gives EMST; 'missing' is a synonym for absent, which serves as the 'case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone such as a ruby or diamond, prized jewel material.

clue.text: Whispers when players enter

indicators.note: the team goes into the word

parts.note: a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: Whispering as the actors come on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors' remarks to the audience, unheard by the other characters, are muttered aside.
